models_evaluated: twelve instruction-tuned LLMs from multiple model families (names not reported in abstract)

links.outcome: LLM recommendation shifts versus neutral control when patient sociodemographic descriptors varied
links.effect: Descriptors changed recommendations; mental health referral lower for Black transgender women (-12.2 pp; 95% CI -14.0 to -10.3), Black homeless patients (-9.1 pp), homeless patients (-7.7 pp); low-income neuroimaging +4.0 pp.
links.quote: Referral likelihood was lower for Black transgender women (-12.2 pp; 95% CI -14.0 to -10.3), Black patients experiencing homelessness (-9.1 pp; -11.0 to -7.3), and patients experiencing homelessness (-7.7 pp; -9.5 to -5.9).

links.outcome: LLM clinical recommendation differences across sociodemographic subgroups
links.effect: Sociodemographic descriptors influenced recommendations, largest for mental health referral in ambiguous cases; attenuated with clearer diagnostic information; other effects smaller.
links.quote: Sociodemographic descriptors influenced LLM recommendations, with the largest differences observed for mental health referral decisions in diagnostically ambiguous cases.

links.outcome: Biased clinical recommendations by patient sociodemographic group in generative AI output
links.effect: LLM recommendations varied by descriptors, particularly under diagnostic uncertainty; referral lower for Black transgender women by 12.2 pp.
links.quote: LLM clinical recommendations varied by sociodemographic descriptors, particularly under diagnostic uncertainty.

unlisted_practices: Providing more detailed, structured clinical information in LLM inputs to reduce sociodemographic bias

screen.reason: Empirical study testing whether providing structured/detailed clinical information mitigates sociodemographic bias in LLM clinical decision-making across synthetic emergency vignettes.

primary.practice: structured clinical input provision to mitigate bias
